answer: A Sybil swarm is priced out by bonding each declared identity to collateral forfeited on proven duplicate control, so every fake persona must carry its own real, slashable value. Verification scans the opal registry for shared owner signals and correlates submitted proofs, building a kernel of control features that clusters suspected aliases. One operator minting thousands of addresses must post the full bond per address, and the detection step is a flat mesa: any alias detected burns the linked set at once, turning the attack into an immediate capital loss with no partial exit.
